text:
sam (PM): Quick sync — now that v1.3 is live, we need a pragmatic plan for post-launch iterations. Focus areas: highest-impact bugs, customer-driven asks, and a small set of enhancements for 1.3.1.

lauren (ENG): I ran through the telemetry. Three regressions jumped out: streaming timeouts (high), embeddings misalignment on long inputs (medium), and an intermittent worker OOM (high).

jordan (TPM): Can we group by customer impact + effort and aim to ship high-impact/high-effort next sprint and low-effort fixes ASAP?

michelle (CS): Customers: Acme and K-Health reported the streaming timeouts during peak. Both on Dedicated. They flagged it as blocking for their demo next week.

raj (SRE): OOM is on a rare sequence length pattern. I can reproduce locally with a 128k token prefix that triggers KV cache growth; will add guardrails.

lauren (ENG): Suggest triage: two hotfixes (streaming timeouts, OOM) -> ship as 1.3.1; embeddings alignment and UX polish -> 1.3.2.

sam (PM): Agree. Let's apply a simple rubric in this thread for consistent decisions. Paste below for votes.

---
```
PRIORITY RUBRIC (quick):
P0: Production crash / data loss / security breach -> immediate hotfix
P1: Paying-customer blocking (demo/contract risk) or severe perf regression -> urgent patch (1.3.1)
P2: Major UX regression or model-quality regression -> next minor (1.3.2)
P3: Low-impact enhancements / backlog -> triage for roadmap
```
---

michelle (CS): Streaming timeouts -> P1 (customer-blocking) :thumbsup:

lauren (ENG): Worker OOM -> P1 (stability)

raj (SRE): OOM mitigation plan: short-term: cap KV cache growth and reject >X tokens with 429 + doc link. Long-term: memory-aware eviction and improved batching. I'll open infra PRs.

sam (PM): embeddings misalignment -> P2 (needs data and evals). We should lock down a test-suite run across quantized variants.

jordan (TPM): For scope negotiation: propose two lanes — "hotfix lane" (1.3.1) and "follow-on lane" (1.3.2). Hotfix lane gets triage, QA sign-off, and optional canary. Follow-on lane will have UX grooming and acceptance criteria.

lauren (ENG): Hotfix tasks I propose:
- fix/streaming-timeout: reduce socket read timeout fallback, add metrics
- fix/oom-guard: reject huge prefixes, add memory probe
- test/ci: add deterministic load test reproducer

michelle (CS): Can we surface to customers which release will include their fixes? I'd prefer clear ETA: hotfix by Tue next week.

sam (PM): ETA target: hotfix branch cut today, canary Wed morning, global rollout Thu if canary OK. That buys our CS team time.

raj (SRE): Ops-bot: scheduling canary.

ops-bot: Scheduled canary for 1798080000 (Wed 08:00 UTC) on dedicated-capacity pool alpha. Health checks: 200/5m, latency p95 < 250ms, error rate < 0.5%.

jordan (TPM): Backlog grooming items for 1.3.2 (candidate):
- enhancement: prompt-template library improvements (low effort)
- enhancement: per-route cost-estimator in console (med effort)
- bug: embeddings drift on long context (med effort)
- doc: private deployment quickstart fixes (low)

sam (PM): Let's cap 1.3.2 scope: no more than 3 medium/1 high items. Everything else goes into "post-1.3.2 backlog". Agree/disagree?

lauren (ENG): Agree. We also need to set launch criteria for each follow-on item. Example: embeddings alignment -> must pass eval suite (recall >= 0.92 on anchor set) and zero regressions on small-quant models.

michelle (CS): From CS perspective: prioritize console cost-estimator and the prompt-template fix (customers asked for both).

raj (SRE): If we add the cost-estimator we need to ensure telemetry doesn't add load to router. Plan: precompute per-route estimates in batch.

sam (PM): Action items:
- lauren: PRs for streaming timeout + OOM guard (today)
- raj: canary schedule + memory probe instrumentation (today)
- michelle: notify Acme + K-Health with ETA and canary details (today)
- jordan: create 1.3.2 epic and add acceptance criteria (today)

lauren (ENG): I'll open the fix PRs and mark them with label `hotfix/1.3.1`. Will also include a small integration test snippet:

```bash
# reproducer for streaming timeout
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"'"$(python -c 'print("x"*65536)')"'"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

michelle (CS): Noting that if canary fails we do rollback + postmortem. CS will draft customer-facing note templates.

jordan (TPM): One more: we should tag all items in backlog with `impact:customer` or `impact:internal` so PM prioritization is data-driven. I'll add that to grooming checklist.

sam (PM): OK. We'll meet tomorrow 09:30 to review canary metrics and finalize 1.3.2 scope. If anything urgent pops, thread updates here. Thanks all. :rocket:

michelle (CS): Thanks. I'll ping when customers acknowledge.

lauren (ENG): PRs opened: #4123, #4124. Marking them ready for review.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for branch hotfix/1.3.1 at 1798040000.

raj (SRE): I'll post canary dashboards link in tomorrow's check-in.

sam (PM): Closing this thread for active syncing — will reopen if blockers.
